sentences.text:
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner No.1 Sudarshan Yadav @ Sudershan Yadav submitted that this interlocutory application has been filed on behalf of the petitioner No.1 for enlarging him on bail during pending of this appeal, which has been preferred against the judgment dated 21st January 2023, passed learned Additional Sessions Judge - II, Deoghar in Criminal Appeal No. 40 of 2016, whereby and whereunder the learned appellant court dismissed the appeal and uphold the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 21st March, 2016 of the petitioner no. 1 under Sections 420/34, 467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, which was passed by learned Sub- Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Madhupur in G.R. Case No. 607 of 1990 Madhupur P.S.
Case No. 117 of 1990, arising out of P.C.R. Case No. 08 of 1989, whereby and whereunder petitioner no. 1 had been convicted under Sections 420/34, 467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced the petitioner no. 1 to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of 02 years with fine of Rs. 2000/- under Section 420/34 of Indian Penal Code, rigorous imprisonment for a period of 03 years with fine of Rs. 2000/- under Section 467 of the Indian Penal Code, rigorous imprisonment for a period of 2 and half years with fine of Rs. 2000/- under Section 468 of the Indian Penal Code and, rigorous imprisonment for a period of 3 years under Section 471 of the Indian Penal Code and in default of paying fine, to undergo simple imprisonment of 3 months.

sentences.text: The gist of the charges levelled against the petitioner No.1 is that he is said to have executed a forged and fabricated sale-deed and for which, the title suit was also filed by the complainant-informant and therefore in this view of the matter, it is submitted that it is a civil nature of dispute and no criminal offence is made out.

Further it has been submitted that neither the learned trial court nor the appellate court has appreciated the evidences adduced on behalf of the prosecution in the right perspective despite the fact that the title suit is pending with respect to the same sale deed in question and that title suit has already been decided and the appeal is also pending before the concerned court and there was no occasion for holding the guilt of the accused petitioner No1. for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 read with Section 34 of IPC.

Further it has also been pointed out that the petitioner No.1 is in custody since 09.05.2023 and he is suffering from several terminating ailments as Prostratomegaly, Bladder Trabeculation,
Kidney Cysts, Thickened Urinary Bladder, etc. and the petitioner No1.

is also suffering with acute illness related to non-passage of urine and was treated in Jagdamba Clinic, Madhupr as well as examined in Deoghar for his ailments in the month of April 2023 and therefore petitioner No.1 deserves to be enlarged on bail, as this criminal revision is not likely to be heard in near future.
4.

On the other hand, learned APP appearing on behalf of the State submitted that both the courts below have consistently found the guilt of the accused petitioner No.1 and therefore he does not deserve to be enlarged on bail.
5. Having heard the parties, perused the record of this case.
6. In view of the persuasive submissions advanced on behalf of the petitioner No.1, it is found just and proper to enlarge the petitioner No.1 Sudarshan Yadav @ Sudershan Yadav on bail.

7. Accordingly, petitioner No.1 Sudarshan Yadav @ Sudershan Yadav is directed to be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the court of learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Madhupur in G.R. Case No.607 of 1990,
Madhupr P.S. Case No.117 of 1990 arising out of PCR Case No.08 of 1989, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. and further subject to the condition that the half of the fine amount under all heads / counts as awarded by the learned court below, that comes to Rs.3,000/- (Rupees three thousands only) shall be deposited by the petitioner No.1 before the learned court below.
8.
Petitioner No.1 is directed to submit the money receipt of the same before this Court.
9. Accordingly, IA. No.4676 of 2023 is allowed.

10. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner seeks to withdraw the I.A. No.4318 of 2023.
11.
As prayed for I.A. No.4318 of 2023
